item.title: [New] File Integrity Monitoring in Defender for Servers: enabling or changing it now needs Owner and Security Admin on the subscription that holds the Log Analytics workspace
item.description:
File Integrity Monitoring is a detection control: whoever can change its rules can stop the monitoring of a registry key or a system path before tampering with it. The page now places that right at subscription Owner plus Security Admin rather than a workspace-level owner, and it now names changing the configuration, not only switching it on and off.

Azure · List who holds Owner and Security Admin on the subscription that contains the FIM Log Analytics workspace and confirm each is expected; alert on Defender for Servers settings writes (Microsoft.Security/pricings) in the Azure Activity log for that subscription; give SOC analysts who only read FIM results the Security Reader role.

item.title: [New] Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider extension for Arc-enabled Kubernetes retires on 9 October 2027; the Secret Store extension replaces it
item.description:
The retiring extension mounts Key Vault secrets through a CSI driver with a service principal credential held on the cluster; its replacement drops that stored credential and instead keeps a copy of every secret in the Kubernetes secret store. The credential risk goes down and the exposure of the secrets to cluster RBAC, audit and etcd encryption goes up, so the migration is a security review and not a version bump.

Azure · List Arc-enabled clusters carrying extension type microsoft.azurekeyvaultsecretsprovider (az k8s-extension list), plan the switch-over window Microsoft describes, confirm encryption at rest and RBAC on Kubernetes Secrets before migrating, and revoke the old service principal on the vault when the migration is done. Clusters in Azure Government or Azure China have no replacement stated yet.
